overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic marine layer morning with patchy coastal fog and a flat temperature profile overnight — the running max is only 64.4°F as of ~7:54 AM PDT, and hourly obs show temperatures locked in the 62–64°F band all night with near-zero velocity right now. The day is trending cooler than the broader regional pattern (extreme heat warnings are confined to inland desert zones well east of the coast), and the onshore flow with SW winds is keeping coastal LA mild. Fog is expected to burn off by 11 AM PDT, allowing some afternoon solar heating.
forecast_obs_notes: The three NWP models show moderate agreement in the 67–70°F range (NBM 67.0, ECMWF 68.4, HRRR 70.2), all within ~3°F of each other and consistent with the NWS forecast of 'high near 69°F.' The INTRADAY model is projecting a slightly earlier peak (~11:42 AM PDT at 14.7h ET) than the NWP consensus (17–18h ET, i.e., 2–3 PM PDT), which likely reflects the current flat trend; the NWP timing is more physically plausible given marine layer burn-off dynamics.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 64.4°F and roughly 5–6 hours of warming potential remaining (fog clearing by 11 AM PDT, peak expected 2–3 PM PDT per NWP models), a rise of ~4–6°F to the mid-to-upper 60s or near 70°F is expected. The META model's top probability is in the 70–71°F bucket (23%), with secondary mass at 72–75°F and 66–67°F, but the NWS and model mean converge around 68–69°F. The active severe weather alerts (extreme heat, Red Flag) are all inland/desert and do not meaningfully affect coastal LA today. Best estimate is approximately 69°F, with the main uncertainty being how quickly and fully the marine layer clears — confidence is moderate.
